version.changelog: Exec steps with confirmation, persistent workflows to files, simplified build/execute flow.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed workflow-automation skill that saves user-approved workflows and requires confirmation before higher-risk shell or file actions.

dimensions.detail: Workflow execution may use network/API calls, agent tools, shell commands, and file writes, which are powerful capabilities, but they are expected for the workflow-builder purpose and shell/file steps require explicit per-step confirmation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains only artifact/SKILL.md and no executable scripts or dependencies; the install text is a normal clawhub install command plus an optional command advertising related skills.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The invocation wording is broad and could route some generic automation requests into this skill, but the artifact frames workflow creation and execution as user-directed and includes approval prompts before saving or running workflows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists workflows under memory/workflows/{name}.md for reuse and auto-creates that directory; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with no evidence of hidden memory modification, background services, hooks, or system persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to plan, save, and execute multi-step workflows; the described capabilities of API calls, agent actions, shell commands, file writes, branching, and saved workflow files fit that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want the agent to create reusable workflow files and help run multi-step automations. Review saved workflows before running them, and be especially cautious approving shell commands, file writes, or workflows that call external APIs or send messages.
llm.findings:
[RA2] expected: The artifact does persist workflows to files, but only after user approval and in a named workflow directory; no background execution, hidden persistence, or modification of agent memory files is described.
[SQP-1] expected: The description is broad because the skill is intended for workflow planning and automation; this increases accidental-use risk but is not purpose-mismatched or deceptive in the artifact.
[SQP-1] expected: The quick command "lag workflow" is generic, but it starts workflow building rather than silent execution, and later save/run actions require user approval or confirmation.
